thread.title: Netflix, Amazon making more scripted shows than broadcasters for the first time

author: Annlee Ellingson
title: Netflix, Amazon making more scripted shows than broadcasters for the first time
text: – Staff Writer, L.A. Biz Dec 14, 2018, 10:29am PST The television industry produced a record 495 original scripted television programs this year, according to a new industry report from FX Networks Research. Of those, 160 — or nearly a third — came from “online services” such as Netflix, Amazon and Hulu, marking the first time that streaming services’ output of scripted originals outpaced that of the broadcast, basic cable and premium cable networks. By comparison, the broadcast networks such as ABC, CBS, the CW, Fox and NBC produced 146 scripted originals; basic cable 144; and premium cable 45. To put the surge in streaming in perspective, digital originals made their first appearance in 2011, when there were just a half-dozen. Here are more recent stories on the streaming industry reported by The Business Journals and elsewhere: WarnerMedia finds creative chief for streaming service Kevin Reilly is taking a bigger role at WarnerMedia as the media conglomerate, now owned by AT&T (NYSE: T), prepares to launch its video platform next year. The television veteran, who serves as president of TBS and TNT and chief creative officer for Turner, has added direct-to-consumer to his purview. He now serves as chief creative officer of direct-to-consumer as well. ( L.A. Biz ) DAZN takes a swing at pay-per-view, but combat sports is just a start In a 30-second commercial spot that aired nationally during NFL, NBA and college football telecasts in recent weeks, iconic ring announcer Michael Buffer reads from an index card, trumpeting DAZN’s broadcast of Canelo Alvarez’s Dec. 15 fight against little-known Brit Rocky Fielding. DAZN, the recently launched direct-to-consumer network, will offer the bout for free to viewers who sign up for a 30-day trial of the service. ( L.A. Biz ) Smithsonian launches new subscription streaming service CBS Corp. (NYSE: CBS) is adding yet another brand to its lineup of subscription streaming services. Smithsonian Networks, a joint venture between CBS-owned Showtime and the Smithsonian Institution, is launching Smithsonian Channel Plus, an ad-free platform featuring more than a thousand hours of content from the network. ( L.A. Biz ) Apple planning big SoCal expansions in San Diego and Culver City Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL) said it's planning big expansions in San Diego and Culver City in Southern California. Apple said that over the next three years, it will expand to more than 1,000 employees in Seattle, San Diego and Culver City each. ( L.A. Biz ) Netflix, Amazon lead SAG Awards TV nominations, flop in film race Netflix Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. dominated the Screen Actors Guild Awards nominations for television on Tuesday morning but were just about shut out of the motion picture race. Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX) garnered 15 nods in TV categories — nearly double any other network, while Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) had the second most with eight. ( L.A. Biz ) Netflix reveals its most popular originals Netflix viewers love romantic comedies. The most popular original Netflix movies (as measured by numbers who rewatched) are "The Kissing Booth" and "To All the Boys I've Loved Before," according to data released by the streaming service on Tuesday. ( Bizwomen ) Netflix is testing an instant scene-replay feature Did that scene in “Black Panther” or “Stranger Things” wow you so much that you wanted to stop everything and instantly rewatch it? A new feature being tested by Netflix could give viewers the ability to do exactly that. ( Los Angeles Times ) Inside Jeffrey Katzenberg’s plan to spend up to $1B by 2025 on programming for Quibi Jeffrey Katzenberg has been open about his plans to spend big bucks on programming for Quibi, his upcoming subscription mobile video streaming service. A pitch deck for investors shared by Quibi earlier this year — back when it was still called “New TV” — shines a light on how Katzenberg, Quibi CEO Meg Whitman and the company will approach the content market. ( Digiday ) Also: Jeffrey Katzenberg -led startup Quibi hires former DC boss Diane Nelson as head of operations ( Deadline ) Music streaming company Spotify flees Mid-Market over safety concerns Spotify (NYSE: SPOT) has broken its lease at 988 Market St., the Mid-Market building home to the Warfield concert venue, and moved to the Merchants Exchange Building in the Financial District due in part to concerns about employee safety at its former location. ( San Francisco Business Times ) Sinclair looks to create a ‘STIRR’ with its new streaming service Sinclair Broadcast Group Inc. is close to launching its new streaming app that executives see as a major opportunity to drive advertising revenue for the broadcaster. Hunt Valley-based Sinclair (NASDAQ: SBGI) has been developing STIRR for more than a year and plans to make it available to the public in early 2019. The app will be ad-supported and free to all users. ( Baltimore Business Journal ) Subscriber content Fandor lays off staff, restructures assets of indie-film streaming service under new entity Fandor, the independent-film streaming service, has laid off nearly all of its employees and transferred its assets to a new entity that’s seeking a buyer. Reached for comment, Fandor CEO/chairman Chris Kelly sent a statement in which he said Fandor has a deal in place that will let a “new entity” continue to operate the service. ( Variety )
